items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: They listen to Cat Anderson, Maynard Ferguson.

ctx.x: The first ARmstrong record I ever copied was "When You're Smiling," which goes up to a high E on the trumpet. In those days if the trumpet player could play up to a high C they thought it was pretty phenomenal. So it was kind of lucky for me that I listened to Louis Armstrong. I didn't know that the trumpet was supposed to stop at C so when I was in high school I could play up to high G. Because it's a matter of your attitude, how high you play, basically. You know, just as young guys come along now, they think…
tell you what they are if I hear them. But, you know, the younger players, many of them think high. They listen to Cat Anderson, Maynard Ferguson.

I was just wondering, that was pretty advanced to be able to copy. Most youngsters couldn't copy those things. You must have had an extremely good ear and a lot of patience to keep playing this record over again.
